### Q11. In PQRST pain assessment, what does R commonly represent?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Respiratory rate only
- **B.** Recovery score
- **C.** Region and radiation
- **D.** Renal function

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Region and radiation**

PQRST ek structured symptom assessment mnemonic hai. P provocation/palliation, Q quality, R region/radiation, S severity aur T timing ko refer karta hai. Region se pata chalta hai pain kahan hai. Radiation batata hai kya pain kisi aur area tak ja raha hai. In findings ko associated symptoms aur examination ke saath interpret karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Respiratory rate vital sign hai, lekin PQRST ka R usually respiratory rate nahi hai.
- **B (Galat):** Recovery score recovery assessment ka tool ho sakta hai, lekin PQRST ka R nahi hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Region aur radiation pain ki location aur spread ko describe karte hain. Yeh correct mnemonic expansion hai.
- **D (Galat):** Renal function relevant investigation ho sakti hai, par mnemonic ka R yeh nahi batata.

**Exam clue:** R = Region and Radiation.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/30-4-pain-assessment)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q15. A patient reports burning, electric-shock pain after nerve injury. Which pain mechanism is most likely?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Referred pain proven by the description alone
- **B.** Normal absence of pain sensation
- **C.** Purely visceral nociceptive pain in every case
- **D.** Neuropathic pain

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Neuropathic pain**

Neuropathic pain tab ho sakti hai jab somatosensory nervous system, yani sensation carry karne wala system, disease ya injury se affected ho. Damaged nerves abnormal signals bhej sakti hain. Burning, shooting aur electric-shock jaisi sensations is mechanism ka clue hain. Nurse sensory changes aur injury history assess karti hai. Sirf description se diagnosis final nahi hota.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Referred pain ka matlab source se different location par pain feel hona hai. Diye gaye descriptors alone referred pain prove nahi karte.
- **B (Galat):** Patient painful sensation report kar raha hai, isliye absence of pain iska meaning nahi hai.
- **C (Galat):** Visceral nociceptive pain internal organs ke pain receptors se arise hoti hai. Nerve injury ke context ko purely visceral kehna appropriate nahi hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Nerve injury ke saath burning aur electric-shock pain neuropathic mechanism suggest karti hai.

**Exam clue:** Burning and electric shocks after nerve injury suggest neuropathic pain.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/30-1-the-pain-process)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q57. A patient has severe new abdominal pain despite normal heart rate and blood pressure. Which response is appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Dismiss pain because vital signs are normal
- **B.** Delay assessment until tachycardia develops
- **C.** Assume the patient wants attention
- **D.** Accept the pain report and assess possible serious causes

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Accept the pain report and assess possible serious causes**

New severe abdominal pain serious illness ka symptom ho sakta hai, even jab heart rate aur BP normal hon. Physiological response patient, timing aur medicines se vary karta hai. Nurse pain report accept karke onset, site, character, abdominal findings, vomiting, bleeding aur other red flags assess karti hai. Urgent clinical review arrange karo aur deterioration monitor karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Normal vital signs severe pain ya dangerous abdominal condition ko rule out nahi karte.
- **B (Galat):** Tachycardia aane tak wait karne se important diagnosis delay ho sakti hai.
- **C (Galat):** Attention-seeking assume karne se real illness miss ho sakti hai. Patient report ko objectively assess karo.
- **D (Sahi):** Pain ko accept karke serious causes evaluate karna patient-centered aur safe response hai.

**Exam clue:** Normal vital signs do not rule out severe pain or serious disease.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/30-4-pain-assessment)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q85. Which assessment is the most reliable starting point for pain intensity in a patient who can communicate?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** The location of the hospital bed
- **B.** The nurse's estimate based on facial expression alone
- **C.** The patient's self-report using a suitable scale
- **D.** Blood pressure alone

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. The patient's self-report using a suitable scale**

Pain ek personal experience hai. Agar patient communicate kar sakta hai toh intensity ka sabse useful starting point uska apna report hai. Suitable scale patient ki language aur understanding ke hisaab se choose karo. Nurse location, onset, quality, function, associated symptoms aur possible cause bhi assess karti hai. Patient ka report respect karne ka matlab serious causes ki assessment skip karna nahi hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Bed ki location pain intensity ke baare mein reliable information nahi deti.
- **B (Galat):** Facial expression useful additional clue hai, lekin kuch patients severe pain mein bhi grimace nahi karte.
- **C (Sahi):** Patient apne experience ko suitable scale se bata sakta hai, isliye yeh best starting point hai.
- **D (Galat):** BP pain, medicines aur bahut saare doosre factors se change ho sakta hai. Isse intensity alone establish nahi hoti.

**Exam clue:** Self-report first when possible, clinical assessment alongside.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/30-4-pain-assessment)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q41. Which pain scale commonly uses numbers from 0 to 10 for a patient who can understand numerical ratings?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Apgar score
- **B.** Numeric rating scale
- **C.** Glasgow Coma Scale
- **D.** Braden Scale

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Numeric rating scale**

Numeric rating scale ya NRS patient ko number se intensity express karne deti hai. Common 0–10 scale mein 0 no pain aur 10 worst imaginable pain ko represent karta hai. Patient se scale ka meaning confirm karo. Reassessment mein same appropriate scale aur functional goal use karne se response compare kar sakte hain.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Apgar score newborn ki immediate adaptation assess karta hai, adult pain rating nahi.
- **B (Sahi):** Numeric rating scale 0–10 numbers use karti hai aur suitable communicative patients ke liye appropriate hai.
- **C (Galat):** Glasgow Coma Scale consciousness ko assess karti hai. Yeh pain intensity score nahi hai.
- **D (Galat):** Braden Scale pressure injury risk assess karti hai, pain intensity nahi.

**Exam clue:** NRS = pain 0–10, not GCS or Braden.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/30-4-pain-assessment)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q79. A patient has a patient-controlled analgesia pump. Which teaching is most appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Press repeatedly on behalf of an unresponsive patient
- **B.** Disable the prescribed lockout interval
- **C.** Only the patient should activate the dose button unless a specifically authorized protocol applies
- **D.** Family should press the button whenever the patient sleeps

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Only the patient should activate the dose button unless a specifically authorized protocol applies**

Patient-controlled analgesia ya PCA ek programmed pump hai jisme patient prescribed bolus request karta hai. Lockout ka matlab dose ke baad set interval tak next bolus automatically nahi milti. Patient ka alert enough hona ek safety protection hai. Unauthorized proxy dosing is protection ko bypass kar sakti hai. Nurse pump settings, pain, sedation aur breathing monitor karti hai. Special clinician-controlled analgesia sirf explicitly authorized separate protocol ke under hoti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Unresponsive patient ko proxy bolus dene ki jagah urgent airway, breathing aur sedation assessment chahiye.
- **B (Galat):** Prescribed lockout disable karne se repeated doses aur overdose ka risk badhta hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Routine PCA button sirf patient press kare. Special authorized protocol ko routine family dosing se confuse mat karo.
- **D (Galat):** Sleeping patient ke behalf par family ka button press karna sedation aur respiratory depression ka risk badha sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** PCA: patient presses, lockout stays enabled.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/30-5-pain-management)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q111. Which nonpharmacological measure can supplement prescribed postoperative pain treatment?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Positioning, relaxation and suitable incision support
- **B.** Force painful exercise without assessment
- **C.** Withhold every prescribed analgesic
- **D.** Apply uncontrolled heat to an insensate area

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Positioning, relaxation and suitable incision support**

Postoperative pain incision aur tissue inflammation se ho sakti hai. Positioning uncomfortable tension kam kar sakti hai. Gentle relaxation anxiety aur muscle tension kam karne mein help karti hai. Coached incision support movement ya coughing ko easier bana sakti hai. Ye measures individualized analgesic plan ko supplement karte hain, replace nahi.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Safe positioning, relaxation aur suitable incision support multimodal comfort plan ke useful components hain.
- **B (Galat):** Painful exercise force karne se patient injure ho sakta hai. Activity plan assessment-based hona chahiye.
- **C (Galat):** Prescribed analgesia automatically withhold karna unnecessary pain aur poor function ka risk badha sakta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Insensate skin temperature injury notice nahi kar paati. Uncontrolled heat burn kar sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Combine non-drug measures with indicated analgesia.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/medical-surgical-nursing/pages/27-2-postoperative-pain-management)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

[Source topic bank: Pain, rest, sleep and comfort therapy, Q8](../MCQs/17-Pain-Rest-Sleep-and-Comfort-Therapy-20-MCQs.md)

Original topic Q8.

### Q119. Following opioid administration, a patient has worsening sedation before respiratory rate falls markedly. Which action is most appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Give another opioid because the patient is quiet
- **B.** Stop all monitoring once pain improves
- **C.** Treat sedation as proof of ideal pain control
- **D.** Assess respiratory status and sedation urgently and follow the opioid safety protocol

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Assess respiratory status and sedation urgently and follow the opioid safety protocol**

Opioids brain ke breathing drive ko suppress kar sakte hain. Increasing sedation, yani patient ka progressively zyada drowsy ya difficult to arouse hona, respiratory depression se pehle warning ho sakti hai. Nurse responsiveness, breathing rate, depth, oxygenation aur appropriate ventilation monitoring urgently assess karti hai. Further opioid safety protocol ke hisaab se hold/review karo aur urgent help ya naloxone as indicated arrange karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Quiet patient oversedated ho sakta hai. Additional opioid breathing ko aur depress kar sakti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Pain improve hone par bhi adverse effects develop ho sakte hain. Monitoring continue honi chahiye.
- **C (Galat):** Sedation adequate analgesia ka reliable proof nahi hai. Excessive sedation unsafe ho sakti hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Urgent assessment aur opioid safety protocol preventable deterioration ko identify aur treat karne mein help karte hain.

**Exam clue:** Increasing sedation after opioid = respiratory safety check, not extra opioid.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://www.apsf.org/article/using-the-2018-guidelines-from-the-joint-commission-to-kickstart-your-hospitals-program-to-reduce-opioid-induced-ventilatory-impairment/)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q35. A patient reports difficulty falling asleep due to repeated noise and nighttime interruptions. Which intervention addresses the likely modifiable cause?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Automatically prescribe a sedative without assessment
- **B.** Provide stimulating activities at midnight
- **C.** Increase overhead lighting throughout the night
- **D.** Reduce nonessential noise and coordinate routine care around rest periods

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Reduce nonessential noise and coordinate routine care around rest periods**

Hospital mein alarms, conversations, lights aur unnecessary interruptions sleep ko fragment kar sakte hain. Patient se specific causes poochho. Nonessential noise kam karo, lights suitable rakho aur routine care ko coordinate karo. Essential observations, time-critical medicines aur safety monitoring postpone nahi karni chahiye. Pain aur breathing problems bhi assess karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Bina assessment sedative prescription appropriate nahi hai aur nursing authorization limits apply hoti hain.
- **B (Galat):** Midnight stimulation sleep onset ko delay kar sakti hai.
- **C (Galat):** Bright light biological sleep-wake cues disturb kar sakti hai. Safety ke liye suitable low lighting preferable ho sakti hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Noise reduction aur safe care coordination stated modifiable environmental cause ko address karti hai.

**Exam clue:** Protect sleep without omitting essential clinical care.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/sleep-deprivation/healthy-sleep-habits)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q105. Which finding is most typical of REM sleep?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** No cerebral activity
- **B.** Continuous high skeletal muscle tone in every person
- **C.** Rapid eye movements and markedly reduced skeletal muscle tone
- **D.** Complete cessation of respiration

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Rapid eye movements and markedly reduced skeletal muscle tone**

REM ka full form rapid eye movement hai. Is stage mein eyes rapidly move kar sakti hain aur brain activity relatively active hoti hai. Most skeletal muscles ka tone markedly reduced hota hai, jise atonia kehte hain. Breathing aur essential muscle activity continue rehti hai. Dreaming REM mein common hai, lekin dreams sirf REM tak limited nahi hain.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** REM mein cerebral activity absent nahi hoti. Brain active reh sakta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Most skeletal muscles mein tone reduce hota hai. Universal sustained high tone typical REM nahi hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Rapid eye movements aur reduced skeletal muscle tone REM ki characteristic findings hain.
- **D (Galat):** Respiration continue rehti hai, although pattern variable ho sakta hai. Complete cessation normal REM feature nahi hai.

**Exam clue:** REM = active brain, rapid eye movements, reduced skeletal tone.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/sleep/stages-of-sleep)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

[Source topic bank: Pain, rest, sleep and comfort therapy, Q10](../MCQs/17-Pain-Rest-Sleep-and-Comfort-Therapy-20-MCQs.md)

### Q107. Which sleep hygiene instruction is generally appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Drink strong coffee immediately before bed
- **B.** Use the bed primarily for stimulating activities
- **C.** Maintain a regular sleep-wake schedule and limit late caffeine
- **D.** Change sleep time by several hours every day

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Maintain a regular sleep-wake schedule and limit late caffeine**

Circadian rhythm body ki internal clock hai jo sleep aur wakefulness timing regulate karti hai. Consistent sleep-wake schedule is rhythm ko stable rakhne mein help karta hai. Caffeine ek stimulant hai jo alertness maintain kar sakti hai. Isliye late caffeine aur bedtime stimulation limit karna generally useful hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Bedtime par strong coffee alertness badha kar sleep onset delay kar sakti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Stimulating activities bed ko wakefulness se associate kar sakti hain. Bed ko rest ke liye use karna helpful hota hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Regular schedule aur late caffeine restriction healthy sleep habits ke consistent hain.
- **D (Galat):** Roz several hours timing change karne se regular body-clock cues disturb ho sakte hain.

**Exam clue:** Consistent timing, quiet environment, limit late caffeine.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/sleep-deprivation/healthy-sleep-habits) · [Clinical reference 2](https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/insomnia/treatment)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q110. A patient is scheduled for a painful dressing change and has an appropriate prescribed analgesic. What is the best planning approach?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Coordinate analgesic timing with expected onset before the procedure
- **B.** Double the dose without authorization
- **C.** Administer it only after the procedure in every case
- **D.** Skip reassessment because pain is anticipated

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Coordinate analgesic timing with expected onset before the procedure**

Analgesic onset ka matlab dose dene ke baad effect start hone ka expected time hai. Painful dressing change plan karte waqt route, medication onset, prescribed dose, patient risk aur previous response consider karo. Procedure se pehle sufficient time par authorized analgesia dene se avoidable pain kam ho sakta hai. Procedure ke dauran aur baad response aur adverse effects reassess karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Expected onset ke saath prescribed analgesic timing coordinate karna proactive pain management hai.
- **B (Galat):** Unauthorized dose doubling overdose aur adverse effects ka risk create karti hai.
- **C (Galat):** Har baar procedure ke baad hi analgesia dene se procedure-related pain prevent karne ka chance miss hota hai.
- **D (Galat):** Expected pain hone se reassessment ki zaroorat khatam nahi hoti. Effectiveness aur safety dono check karo.

**Exam clue:** Premedicate according to authorized dose and onset, then reassess.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/30-4-pain-assessment)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q8. Which physiological effect is commonly associated with local cold application?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Permanent loss of all sensation
- **B.** Increased local metabolism without limit
- **C.** Vasoconstriction and reduced local metabolic activity
- **D.** Immediate sustained vasodilation in every case

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Vasoconstriction and reduced local metabolic activity**

Local controlled cold se blood vessels commonly narrow hoti hain. Is process ko vasoconstriction kehte hain. Tissue metabolic activity aur nerve conduction temporarily slow ho sakti hain, jisse pain aur swelling selected conditions mein kam ho sakte hain. Response exposure, tissue condition aur duration par depend karta hai. Excessive cold harmful hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Permanent sensation loss desired therapeutic outcome nahi hai. Yeh tissue ya nerve injury indicate kar sakta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Cold usually metabolism slow karti hai, unlimited increase expected nahi hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Vasoconstriction aur reduced local metabolic activity controlled cooling ke common physiological effects hain.
- **D (Galat):** Immediate sustained vasodilation universal cold response nahi hai. Prolonged exposure mein vascular response change ho sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** Cold = vasoconstriction and slower local activity.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/medical-surgical-nursing/pages/7-4-nonpharmacological-pain-management)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q52. An older postoperative patient snores loudly, has witnessed pauses in breathing and receives sedatives. Which concern deserves assessment?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Normal sleep that requires no observation
- **B.** Possible sleep-disordered breathing with increased respiratory depression risk
- **C.** Proof of complete airway patency
- **D.** An indication to increase sedatives without review

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Possible sleep-disordered breathing with increased respiratory depression risk**

Witnessed apnea ka matlab kisi ne breathing pause observe kiya hai. Loud snoring aur pauses obstructive sleep apnea ya doosri sleep-disordered breathing ka clue ho sakte hain. Postoperative sedatives aur opioids airway tone ya breathing drive ko affect kar sakte hain. Nurse breathing, responsiveness, oxygenation aur appropriate ventilation monitoring assess karti hai aur prompt clinical review leti hai. Diagnosis sirf snoring se confirm nahi hota.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Witnessed pauses ko routine harmless sleep assume karna deterioration miss kar sakta hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Observed pauses aur sedating medicines respiratory risk ko justify karte hain. Assessment aur monitoring appropriate hain.
- **C (Galat):** Snoring narrowed airway ka sign bhi ho sakti hai. Complete patency prove nahi karti.
- **D (Galat):** Additional sedative bina respiratory review risk badha sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Snoring + witnessed pauses + sedatives = assess respiratory risk.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://www.apsf.org/article/using-the-2018-guidelines-from-the-joint-commission-to-kickstart-your-hospitals-program-to-reduce-opioid-induced-ventilatory-impairment/)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q99. A patient with reduced peripheral circulation is prescribed cold therapy. Which safety approach is appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Verify suitability, use protective measures and reassess skin and circulation
- **B.** Cover the site tightly and leave it unobserved
- **C.** Apply ice directly for an unlimited time
- **D.** Assume reduced sensation protects against cold injury

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Verify suitability, use protective measures and reassess skin and circulation**

Cold application tissue temperature kam karti hai aur local blood vessels narrow kar sakti hai. Poor peripheral circulation mein tissue ko already limited blood supply mil sakti hai. Reduced sensation ho toh patient excessive cold notice bhi nahi kar paata. Suitability aur contraindications verify karo, approved protective barrier aur duration follow karo aur skin/circulation reassess karo. Concern ho toh application stop karke review lo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Patient-specific suitability, protection aur ongoing assessment correct safety approach hai.
- **B (Galat):** Tight wrapping circulation aur compromise kar sakti hai. Unobserved therapy unsafe hai.
- **C (Galat):** Unlimited direct ice cold injury aur tissue damage ka risk badhati hai.
- **D (Galat):** Reduced sensation injury detect karna mushkil banati hai. Yeh protection nahi hai.

**Exam clue:** Cold therapy: assess perfusion and sensation first.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/medical-surgical-nursing/pages/7-4-nonpharmacological-pain-management)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q100. Which intervention commonly supports comfort in a patient with dry lips and an NPO order?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Give unrestricted water despite the order
- **B.** Provide approved lip and oral care while maintaining aspiration precautions
- **C.** Avoid all oral care
- **D.** Apply an unapproved irritating chemical

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Provide approved lip and oral care while maintaining aspiration precautions**

NPO ka matlab nil per os, yani oral intake restricted hai. Patient ko dry lips aur mouth discomfort ho sakta hai. Approved oral hygiene aur lip care comfort maintain kar sakti hai bina NPO order violate kiye. Patient ki swallowing ability, consciousness, aspiration risk aur specific preprocedure instructions check karo. Suitable suction-assisted care trained staff kar sakta hai if indicated.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Unrestricted water NPO restriction violate kar sakta hai aur aspiration ya procedure safety risk la sakta hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Approved oral and lip care with aspiration precautions comfort aur safety ko balance karti hai.
- **C (Galat):** Oral care avoid karne se dryness, discomfort aur hygiene worsen ho sakte hain.
- **D (Galat):** Unapproved irritating chemical mucosa damage kar sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** NPO does not automatically mean no mouth care.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/25-3-the-nurses-role-in-hygiene)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

## Mock 05

Source: `Chapters/Nursing-Foundations/Mock-Tests/Nursing-Foundations-Mock-05-120.md` (blob `87f47ceb363ef1ba3ec05908b0f610a600c88035`).

### Q10. A patient with acute unexplained unilateral calf swelling requests massage and heat. What should the nurse do?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Assume swelling is harmless if skin is intact
- **B.** Avoid the requested treatment until possible thrombosis and other causes are assessed
- **C.** Massage deeply immediately
- **D.** Apply intense heat without assessment

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Avoid the requested treatment until possible thrombosis and other causes are assessed**

DVT ya deep vein thrombosis mein deep vein ke andar clot ban sakta hai. New unilateral calf swelling aur pain is condition ke possible clues hain, although doosre causes bhi ho sakte hain. Nurse massage aur heat defer karke urgent clinical assessment arrange karti hai. Sudden dyspnea, chest pain ya collapse emergency escalation maangta hai kyunki pulmonary embolism possible hai. Diagnosis clinical evaluation aur indicated tests se hota hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Intact skin se deep vein clot exclude nahi hota.
- **B (Sahi):** Possible thrombosis aur other causes assess hone tak treatment defer karna safest listed approach hai.
- **C (Galat):** Deep massage unexplained painful swelling mein inappropriate hai aur assessment ko delay kar sakti hai.
- **D (Galat):** Intense heat cause ko treat nahi karti aur tissue harm ka risk la sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** New unilateral calf swelling: urgent assessment before massage or heat.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/deep-vein-thrombosis-dvt/)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q12. Which response commonly occurs with suitable local superficial heat application?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Complete cessation of circulation
- **B.** Immediate freezing of tissue
- **C.** Permanent destruction of sensory nerves
- **D.** Vasodilation and improved local blood flow

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Vasodilation and improved local blood flow**

Suitable superficial heat local blood vessels ko widen kar sakti hai. Isse vasodilation kehte hain aur local blood flow increase ho sakta hai. Heat selected muscle stiffness aur discomfort mein relaxation support kar sakti hai. Acute unexplained swelling, impaired sensation ya poor circulation mein suitability verify karo. Approved temperature, barrier aur reassessment follow karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Complete circulation cessation therapeutic goal nahi hai aur tissue ischemia cause kar sakti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Freezing tissue cold exposure ka effect hai, controlled heat ka nahi.
- **C (Galat):** Sensory nerve destruction serious injury hai, normal heat effect nahi.
- **D (Sahi):** Vasodilation aur improved local blood flow suitable heat ke expected effects hain.

**Exam clue:** Heat = vasodilation, but assess safety first.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/medical-surgical-nursing/pages/7-4-nonpharmacological-pain-management)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q53. A patient reports pain reduced from 8/10 to 4/10 after treatment but remains unable to deep breathe. How should the nurse evaluate the intervention?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Automatically repeat every medication dose early
- **B.** Assess both pain relief and functional goal achievement and revise the plan if needed
- **C.** Ignore the breathing limitation
- **D.** Declare complete success from the score alone

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Assess both pain relief and functional goal achievement and revise the plan if needed**

Pain evaluation ka goal sirf number ko kam karna nahi hai. Patient 8/10 se 4/10 tak improve hua, lekin deep breath abhi bhi nahi le paa raha. Nurse functional goal, respiratory status, incision support, sedation aur treatment adverse effects reassess karti hai. Possible serious respiratory problem ho toh prompt review lo. Authorized plan ko response ke according adjust karne ke liye team ke saath communicate karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Medication early repeat karne se dose stacking aur adverse effects ho sakte hain. Authorization aur assessment zaroori hain.
- **B (Sahi):** Pain relief aur function dono evaluate karke plan revise karna comprehensive outcome assessment hai.
- **C (Galat):** Deep breathing limitation postoperative recovery aur respiratory safety ke liye relevant hai.
- **D (Galat):** Score improve hona partial benefit batata hai, complete functional success nahi.

**Exam clue:** Pain score plus function plus safety, not score alone.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/30-4-pain-assessment) · [Clinical reference 2](https://openstax.org/books/medical-surgical-nursing/pages/27-2-postoperative-pain-management)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q57. Which approach supports a patient experiencing persistent anxiety-related tension before sleep?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Offer relaxation breathing and discuss concerns while assessing underlying causes
- **B.** Encourage rapid hyperventilation
- **C.** Guarantee immediate sleep without assessment
- **D.** Dismiss the patient's concerns

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Offer relaxation breathing and discuss concerns while assessing underlying causes**

Anxiety-related tension sleep onset difficult bana sakti hai. Gentle slow breathing aur supportive conversation patient ko relax karne mein help kar sakti hain. Nurse patient ki concerns sunti hai aur pain, breathing symptoms, medicines, environment aur persistent anxiety jaise possible causes assess karti hai. Severe or persistent symptoms par suitable clinical support arrange karo. Sleep immediately aane ka guarantee nahi diya ja sakta.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Relaxation, supportive listening aur cause assessment patient-centered comfort approach hai.
- **B (Galat):** Rapid hyperventilation se dizziness aur discomfort badh sakta hai. Gentle controlled breathing preferable hai.
- **C (Galat):** Immediate sleep guarantee unrealistic hai aur underlying cause miss kar sakti hai.
- **D (Galat):** Concerns dismiss karne se trust aur assessment quality reduce ho sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Support relaxation and assess causes instead of dismissing anxiety.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/30-5-pain-management) · [Clinical reference 2](https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/sleep-deprivation/healthy-sleep-habits)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>
